title: Grid Dynamics acquires Ekumen, deepening expertise in Robotics Product Engineering and Physical AI
summary: Grid Dynamics joins forces with Ekumen, a robotics and physical AI product engineering firm, strengthening its ability to help enterprises build, deploy, and scale intelligent robotic systems.

title: Contango Converts Remaining Hedge Contracts into Debt
summary: FAIRBANKS, Alaska, July 6, 2026 /CNW/ – Contango Silver & Gold Inc. (“Contango” or the “Company”) (NYSE American: CTGO) (TSX: CTGO) is pleased to announce that it has amended its credit facility (the “Amended Credit Facility”) to convert the remaining 15,000 ounces of hedged gold into debt with its existing lenders. body_text: FAIRBANKS, Alaska, July 6, 2026 /CNW/ – Contango Silver & Gold Inc. (“Contango” or the “Company”) (NYSE American: CTGO) (TSX: CTGO) is pleased to announce that it has amended its credit facility (the “Amended Credit Facility”) to convert the remaining 15,000 ounces of hedged gold into debt with its existing lenders. As part of the Amended Credit Facility, the interest rate was reduced to approximately 7.40%. Rick Van Nieuwenhuyse, the Company’s CEO, commented: “We viewed the recent pullback in gold prices as an opportunistic window to completely liquidate our hedge book. By converting the remaining 15,000 ounces of hedge contracts into debt, we have successfully removed the ceiling on our future cash flows from gold production. We are particularly bullish on gold’s macro trajectory from these levels, and our priority is to deliver full, unhedged exposure to rising gold prices directly to Contango shareholders. Operationally, Manh Choh is in a transitional phase as mining transitions from the North Pit to the South Pit and is poised to finish 2026 with higher-grade campaigns, perfectly setting the stage for a record-breaking, fully unhedged production year in 2027. Crucially, we retain the flexibility to repay this debt at any time, and we remain aggressively focused on paying down the credit facility ahead of schedule.” Highlights of the Amended Credit Facility Interest rate reduced to approximately 7.40% from the previous rate of approximately 8.9% No restructuring fee Converted 15,000 hedged gold ounces with an average strike price of $1,935 with maturity dates ranging between March and June 2027 into $33.0 million (“M”) of debt As part of a price protection strategy to offset the hedge settlements, the Company paid $715,000 to purchase 15,000 put contracts with a strike price of $3,100 per ounce with maturities in March and June 2027, which has been added to the debt The total principal of the Amended Credit Facility increased from $12.6 M to $46.3 M, with principal repayments scheduled as follows: September 30, 2026 – $1 M December 31, 2026 – $1 M March 31, 2027 – $15.5 M June 30, 2027 – $28.8 M Conference Call and Webcast Contango will host a conference call and webcast to discuss the hedge conversion with CEO Rick Van Nieuwenhuyse and CFO Mike Clark on Monday, July 6, at 1:00pm EST / 10:00am PST. Participants may join the webcast using the following call-in details: https://6ix.com/event/contango-silver-and-gold-update-on-hedges . ABOUT CONTANGO Contango is an NYSE American and TSX-listed mining company that engages in the exploration for and development of silver, gold, and associated minerals with a growth strategy focused on district-scale silver and gold exploration in British Columbia’s Golden Triangle funded by high-grade gold production in Alaska. The Company’s flagship Canadian asset comprises approximately 247,000 acres (100,000 hectares) of prospective silver-gold mineral tenures in and around the Kitsault Valley, the southern cornerstone of the Golden Triangle. In Alaska, Contango holds a 30% interest in the Peak Gold JV, which leases approximately 675,000 acres of land for production and exploration on the Manh Choh project, with the remaining 70% owned by KG Mining (Alaska), Inc., an indirect subsidiary of Kinross Gold Corporation, operator of the Peak Gold JV. The Company and its subsidiaries also hold: (i) a lease on the Johnson Tract project, which consists of mineral rights to approximately 21,000 acres located near tidewater, 125 miles southwest of Anchorage, Alaska, from the underlying owner, CIRI; (ii) 100% ownership of the Lucky Shot project, which consists of mineral rights to approximately 8,600 acres of State of Alaska and patented mining claims located in the Willow Mining District about 75 miles north of Anchorage, Alaska; (iii) mineral rights to approximately 145,000 acres of State of Alaska mining claims; and (iv) mineral rights to approximately 11,700 acres of State of Alaska mining claims and upland mining leases, all of which give Contango the exclusive right to explore and develop minerals on these lands. Additional information can be found on our web page at www.contangoore.com . FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS This press release contains forward-looking information and forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable securities (“Forward-looking Statements”). These include statements regarding Contango’s plans and expectations for its properties and operations, the content within future annual filings, operations in respect of Contango mineral properties and any benefits of investment in Contango. These Forward-looking Statements also include those relating to the Amended Credit Facility and its terms, the Company’s plans to repay that facility over time and potentially ahead of schedule, the conversion of the Company’s remaining hedges into debt and the resulting unhedged exposure to gold prices, management’s outlook on gold prices, the Company’s price protection strategy, and expectations for mining and production at Manh Choh through 2026 and into 2027. title: W-8 BEN: What It Is, Who Needs It & How to Fill It Out (July 2026)
summary: Get a clear breakdown of the W-8BEN form for July 2026 — who needs it, how to complete each part, and how to avoid triggering the 30% default
body_text: Foreign status paperwork trips up a lot of people, and the W-8BEN is one of those forms that sounds more complicated than it actually is. If you're a nonresident alien earning dividends, royalties, or contractor pay from a U.S. source, you'll need a completed W-8BEN on file before your payer can legally skip that default 30% withholding. Whether you need a current PDF or need to decide between W-8BEN and W-8BEN-E, this guide covers both. TLDR: W-8BEN verifies non-U.S. individual payees; missing it triggers a 30% withholding under IRC §1441. Tax treaties covering roughly 67 countries can cut that 30% rate, sometimes to 0%, via Part II. A signed W-8BEN expires at the end of the third calendar year after signing; status changes void it early. Request W-8BEN for individuals and W-8BEN-E for foreign entities; submitting the wrong form blocks payment. Dots Tax automates W-8BEN collection inside onboarding and tracks the rolling three-year renewal cycle. What the W-8BEN Form Is The Form W-8BEN (foreign status certification forms) verifies that a payee is a non-U.S. individual earning U.S.-sourced income. You must collect this paperwork before paying international contractors. Without a valid W-8BEN on file, IRC §1441 requires you to deduct a default 30% of the earnings. Securing this document prevents that default withholding from hitting your payees unnecessarily: keeping payments whole and your contractor relationships intact. It also shields you from the burden of issuing corrected 1099s or refunding over-withheld amounts at year-end. Collect it before the first payment clears, not after the withholding has already been applied. Who Needs to Complete a W-8BEN You must submit a W-8BEN individual form if you are a nonresident alien receiving United States sourced income. This covers foreign contractors, creators, and international investors earning dividends, royalties, or payouts from a domestic business. This document applies strictly to individuals. Certain groups skip this paperwork entirely: Citizens and resident aliens file W-9s (US tax identification forms) to certify their taxpayer identification number with U.S. payers: the W-8BEN does not apply to them. Permanent residents holding a green card are also treated as U.S. persons for tax purposes and follow the same W-9 path. If you receive a W-8BEN from someone who turns out to be a U.S. person, reject it and request a W-9 instead; submitting the wrong form triggers backup withholding under IRC §3406. W-8BEN vs. W-8BEN-E: Which Form Applies When paying international contractors, request the correct paperwork based on their legal structure. The choice depends on whether the payee operates as a solo worker or a registered business entity. Form Type Target Payee Structural Complexity W-8BEN Individual beneficial owners Three basic parts W-8BEN-E Foreign entities and partnerships Requires FATCA classification and up to 30 additional fields depending on entity type, tax status, and ownership structure How to Complete the W-8BEN Form Learning how to fill out the W-8BEN form in 2026 demands accuracy across three parts. Part I Identification Provide your exact legal name and citizenship country. Enter a physical permanent location strictly within your claimed tax residency country. Post office boxes trigger rejection. Insert your taxpayer identification number. Part II Claim of Tax Treaty Benefits This section lowers withholding liability. Name your country of residence and cite the specific treaty article that authorizes the reduced rate. For example, a contractor in the UK claiming the U.S.-UK treaty on royalties would enter "Article 12" and the applicable reduced rate: often 0%. Leave Part II blank and the payer must default to 30%, even if your country qualifies for a lower rate. Claiming Tax Treaty Benefits on Part II The default U.S. tax withholding for foreign contractors on FDAP (fixed or determinable, annual or periodic) income sits at 30% . Bilateral tax treaties reduce that liability for residents of roughly 67 countries , sometimes to 0%. To claim a reduced rate, complete Part II of the W-8BEN with your country of residence and the specific treaty article that authorizes it. Your payer applies that reduced rate immediately. Without Part II, they must default to 30% regardless of your country's treaty status. Check the IRS's full list of U.S. tax treaty countries before submitting; not every nation qualifies, and rates vary by income type. W-8BEN Validity Period and When to Renew A certified W-8BEN remains active from the signature date through the third succeeding calendar year. Staying on top of contractor tax compliance means tracking these expiration windows carefully. If a contractor signs a W-8BEN form on March 15, 2026 it expires on December 31, 2029. Validity ends early if the payee experiences a status change. Acquiring U.S. residency, obtaining a green card, or relocating to a country where the previously claimed tax treaty no longer applies voids the form immediately. The payee must submit a fresh W-8BEN within 30 days of the change. Until you receive the updated form, apply 30% withholding on all subsequent payments to stay compliant with IRC §1441. Common W-8BEN Mistakes That Trigger 30% Withholding Filing errors force payers to apply maximum backup withholding. Knowing how to fill out a W-8BEN form prevents rejected files and blocked earnings, which is a key step in how to pay independent contractors correctly. Watch for these frequent failures: Skipping Part II defaults the tax liability to 30% even for residents of eligible treaty nations. The submitted name must perfectly match the payee government identification. Any discrepancy (a nickname, middle-name omission, or anglicized spelling) causes the form to fail validation. Ask payees to copy their name exactly as it appears on their passport or national ID before submitting. Using a P.O. box instead of a physical location in Part I triggers automatic rejection. The IRS requires a permanent residential location in the payee's country of tax residency; a mailing-only entry does not satisfy this requirement. Submitting an expired W-8BEN, or failing to recollect one after a status change, forces the payer to apply 30% withholding on every subsequent payment until a valid replacement is on file. Build renewal tracking into your onboarding system so expiration windows never slip past year-end. Where to Download the W-8BEN Form Go to IRS.gov and search "W-8BEN" to reach the official form page. Download the primary form PDF first. Download the instruction sheet as a separate PDF. The IRS publishes the W-8BEN instructions as a standalone document alongside the form. For a scalable approach, see how automating Form 1099 and W-8BEN collection via payout infrastructure reduces manual effort. Always download the current W-8BEN form version directly from IRS.gov instead of reusing a saved copy: the IRS periodically revises the form, and submitting a superseded edition can invalidate the certification. Check the revision date printed in the upper left corner of the form before sending it to a payee. If the date on your copy doesn't match the version currently posted on IRS.gov, discard it and pull a fresh download. How Dots Handles W-8BEN Collection for International Payees Tracking tax documentation for international workers creates compliance risk: missed renewals trigger 30% withholding under IRC §1441. Solutions for automated compliance and tax management in contractor payments solve this directly. A W-8BEN form expires on a rolling three-year cycle. Any change in circumstances requires a fresh submission within 30 days. Missing either deadline triggers 30% backup withholding on every affected payment. We built Dots Tax to automate W-8BEN collection directly inside your onboarding flow. Before a payee's first payment clears, Dots prompts them to complete and submit their W-8BEN with no manual follow-up required. The system tracks each form's three-year validity window and triggers re-collection automatically when a form is approaching expiration or a payee's circumstances change. That means your team never has to audit a spreadsheet for lapsed certifications or retroactively apply 30% withholding because a renewal slipped through the cracks. Final Thoughts on W-8BEN Requirements for Foreign Contractors The form itself is simple. Staying on top of renewals, status changes, and Part II treaty claims across a growing contractor roster is where things get complicated. Get the basics right, stay ahead of expirations, and connect with Dots if you want the whole collection process off your plate. Book a demo with Dots today and automate W-8BEN collection from day one. FAQ How do I fill out the W-8BEN form correctly to avoid the 30% withholding rate? Complete all three parts accurately: enter your exact legal name and a physical location (not a P.O. box) in Part I, claim your applicable tax treaty benefits in Part II, and sign in Part III. Skipping Part II is the single most common error: it locks your withholding at 30% even if your country has a bilateral treaty with the U.S. that reduces it to 0%. W-8BEN vs. W-8BEN-E: Which Form Should I Send to a Foreign Contractor? Send the W-8BEN to individual contractors and sole workers; send the W-8BEN-E to foreign entities, corporations, and partnerships. Getting this wrong means collecting a form the IRS will reject, triggering default 30% backup withholding on every payment until you receive a valid replacement. Where can I download the current W-8BEN form for 2025 or 2026? Download the W-8BEN directly from IRS.gov: search "IRS W-8BEN form download" to reach the official page. Save the instruction sheet as a separate PDF alongside the form itself, since the IRS publishes the W-8BEN instructions as a standalone document. Always pull the current version before sending it to payees, as form revisions supersede prior editions. What's the best way to collect W-8BEN forms at scale without manual follow-up? Automate collection inside your payee onboarding flow instead of chasing forms after payments are already queued. Dots Tax collects W-8BEN certification from non-U.S. payees before their first payout clears, tracks the rolling three-year validity window, and triggers re-collection automatically when a form expires or a payee's circumstances change: cutting the 30% withholding risk at the source instead of catching the gap at year-end. How long does a W-8BEN form remain valid, and what triggers early expiration? A signed W-8BEN stays valid from its signature date through December 31 of the third following calendar year, so a form signed on March 15, 2026 expires December 31, 2029. It expires early if the payee acquires U.S. residency or moves to a country where the claimed treaty no longer applies; in either case, a fresh W-8BEN must be submitted within 30 days of the status change or you must apply 30% withholding on all subsequent payments.

title: Why Agencies Prefer a White Label Ad Management Platform Over Traditional Gimmicks & Guesswork
summary: Why Agencies Prefer a White Label Ad Management Platform Over Traditional Gimmicks & Guesswork by Logan Welbaum
body_text: Are you running an agency and still managing client ads the old way? If yes, you already know how messy it can get. Different tools. Different logins. Different dashboards. And then clients asking for updates all the time. It never really stops. Now think about this instead. One system. One platform. One place where everything sits together. That is what white label ad systems do. They change how agencies work with clients. They make things simpler, faster, and much easier to manage. And this is exactly why more agencies are moving away from traditional ad management and switching to white label platforms like Plai. The Problem With Traditional Ad Management Let’s be honest. Traditional ad management is heavy. You open one tool for Google ads. Another for Meta. Another for reporting. Then you move between sheets, notes, and messages. Now multiply this by ten or twenty clients. You start spending more time managing systems than actually improving campaigns. And clients? They want updates all the time. Some want daily reports. Some want quick changes. Some just want to know what is happening. So you end up stuck in back-and-forth communication all day. This is where things start feeling stressful. Not because ads are hard. But because the system is broken and scattered. What White Label Systems Actually Change Now let’s simplify it. A white label system is basically your own branded platform. Your logo, your name, and your clients log in to your system. Not a third-party tool. Inside that system, everything is connected. Campaigns, reports, tracking, and clients can see everything in real time. So instead of you explaining results again and again, clients just open the dashboard. They see it themselves. That alone removes a lot of pressure from your daily work. One Place for All Client Work If you are managing multiple clients, you know the biggest problem is switching. Switching accounts. Switching tools. Switching tabs. White label platforms fix that. You log into one system and see all your clients in one place and get all the white label marketing tools at one place. Clean and simple. You can check performance. You can launch campaigns. You can update ads. All without jumping around. This saves time. But more than that, it saves your energy. You stop feeling like you are always catching up with tasks. Clients Get a Simpler Experience Too Now think from your client’s side. They don’t want complexity. They don’t care how many tools you are using behind the scenes. They just want results and clarity. With a white label system, they get a clean dashboard. They can see performance anytime. No waiting for reports. No confusion. They feel more connected to the process. And when clients feel informed, they trust you more. That trust is everything in agency work. Less Manual Work, More Focus on Strategy Here is something agencies don’t talk about enough. A lot of time is wasted on repetitive tasks. Downloading reports. Sending updates. Checking numbers across platforms. Copying data into sheets. White label systems reduce all of that. Many things are automated or already shown in real time. So instead of doing manual work all day, you can focus on what actually matters. Strategy. Scaling campaigns. Improving performance. That is where real agency growth happens. Easier Scaling Without Extra Chaos Now let’s talk about growth. Every agency wants more clients. But more clients usually means more stress. Unless your system can handle it. White label platforms are built for scale. You can add new clients quickly. You don’t need to rebuild everything from scratch. You don’t need to create new workflows every time. Everything already exists inside the system. You just plug in new clients and go. That is a big difference compared to traditional methods. Better Control Without Losing Transparency Some agencies worry about control. They feel if clients see everything, it might create questions. But it actually works the opposite way. When clients can see results clearly, they ask fewer questions. Because they already have answers in front of them. And for you, this means fewer support messages, fewer explanations, and fewer misunderstandings. Everything becomes more transparent and stable. Stronger Client Relationships At the end of the day, agency work is about relationships. Not just ads. When clients feel informed and involved, they stay longer. They trust the process more. They feel like they are part of the system, not outside it. White label platforms help build that feeling. They make your agency look more professional and more organised. That leaves a strong impression. Why Agencies Prefer a White Label Platform So now let’s bring it together. Traditional ad management feels scattered. Too many tools. Too much manual work. Too many updates. You jump from platform to platform just to keep things running. It slows everything down and makes simple tasks feel heavy. White label systems change that completely. Everything sits in one place. One platform. One dashboard. One flow for all clients. You don’t waste time switching tools or chasing data anymore. You just log in and see everything clearly. Agencies prefer this way because it saves time in a real way. Not small minutes here and there, but hours every week. It reduces confusion because everyone is looking at the same system. It improves client experience because reports are clean and easy to understand. And it makes scaling much easier without adding extra stress to the team. You can handle more clients without feeling overloaded all the time. This is exactly where Plai AI fits in. Plai gives agencies a simple white-label-style system where they can manage ads, track performance, and handle multiple clients from one dashboard. No switching tools. No scattered workflows.
